title: End or remove one local Account session without silently losing accepted offline work

requirements.invariant: Before ending or removing a local Account session, Ledger produces one exact environment-, Principal-, and Account-scoped summary with separate nonnegative counts for queued operations, applying operations, unresolved rejected operations, and captured attachment bytes whose upload is not verified.
Ordinary clean logout is permitted only from a current all-zero summary. Pending work or a changed summary blocks clean teardown rather than converting accepted work into silent deletion.

Sync-then-logout remains synchronizing while any counted work is pending and becomes teardown-ready only when a fresh same-scope summary proves every operation authoritative or explicitly resolved and every captured attachment verified or explicitly resolved.

Destructive local removal is the sole pending-work discard path. It requires explicit confirmation bound to the exact current scoped summary and counts, invalidates on summary change, and never claims discarded operations or attachments reached the server.

Cancellation creates no end-session request, and prompt closure, token expiry, revocation, app termination or interrupted cleanup is never destructive consent. Teardown orchestration stays behind one AccountSessionEnding boundary and resumes fail-closed.

The target-neutral lifecycle preserves accepted operations/media in their original Account, distinguishes local from authoritative completion, prevents cross-Account reuse, and supplies stable bounded failures without choosing identity-provider, offline-lease or UI policy.

AccountSessionEnding exposes pending-work inspection and one typed clean, sync-first, or explicitly confirmed destructive disposition. Feature code receives no provider object and cannot invoke provider signout, local queue deletion, database/key deletion or cache cleanup independently.

This Phase 1 boundary is executable only with deterministic provider-free evidence while the shipped Firebase app remains unchanged; Auth choice, encrypted physical storage, queue/upload implementation, provider signout, schema/RLS/Sync, app UI, migration, hosted resources and production remain outside the slice.

items: PendingLocalWorkSummary binds target environment, PrincipalID, AccountID, monotonically supplied snapshot revision, finite observation time and four exact UInt64 counts; its fingerprint covers all of that evidence and it derives only whether blocking work exists.

SessionEndDisposition distinguishes ordinary clean logout, synchronize-then-logout and remove-from-device-discarding-pending-work. DestructiveLocalRemovalConfirmation binds explicit confirmation time to one exact summary fingerprint and scope.

SessionEndRequest binds its disposition, exact expected summary, optional destructive confirmation and finite request time in one canonical fingerprint. Construction and decoding revalidate clean-zero and destructive exact-confirmation rules.

SessionEndPolicy compares a request with a fresh current summary: clean and destructive dispositions require exact unchanged summary evidence; sync-first reports synchronization-required until a same-scope zero summary is observed. AccountSessionEnding is the sole narrow provider-neutral teardown port.

SessionEndingFailure exposes stable bounded diagnostic codes for invalid time, pending clean request, missing/mismatched confirmation, scope mismatch, changed summary, fingerprint mismatch, malformed encoding and incomplete synchronization.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This Phase 1 policy creates no Account/session/operation/attachment table, key state, cleanup journal, constraint, index, view or migration.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No Auth callback, sync drain, provider signout, local cleanup coordinator, destructive deletion or server command is implemented.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Supabase Data API relation or function is exposed and no grant is added.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: Typed environment/Principal/Account binding is not authorization. No membership policy, RLS helper, revocation rule or cross-tenant database claim is introduced.

syncStreams.notApplicable: No PowerSync Stream, upload connector, operation/result table, attachment queue, stream revocation or local-row removal behavior is implemented.

items: Summary, confirmation and request evidence is canonical Codable state with deterministic SHA-256 fingerprints and byte-identical restart; decoding reconstructs every scope, time, disposition, count and confirmation invariant.

A fresh summary is mandatory before teardown evaluation. Changed scope, counts, snapshot revision or fingerprint refuses clean/destructive teardown; sync-first may advance only to a fresh same-scope all-zero summary.

A deterministic reference port may prove request/evaluation flow, no-call cancellation and failing-port behavior; it cannot prove encrypted persistence, actual process/device restart, filesystem/key deletion, provider signout, crash recovery or physical offline behavior.

storageMedia.notApplicable: The summary counts unverified captured attachments but owns no bytes, paths, upload, reference detach, retention, quarantine or deletion behavior; O-023 remains open.

appMcp.notApplicable: No logout/disposition screen, exact product copy, settings/root wiring, MCP session command, Auth SDK, transport or app/MCP parity is implemented.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase UID/session/cache/media queue is read, transformed, deleted or migrated. Later adapters must reconcile exact Account-scoped operation/media work before any cleanup.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: Stable local failures are contract values only; no logout/cleanup signal, metric, alert, audit sink or recovery runbook execution is activated.

items: Implementation remains inside provider-free LedgerTargetCore and its tests and does not change or link either application project.

The slice cannot authenticate, choose an Auth provider, decide offline lease/reauthorization, synchronize work, delete queues/media/database/key/cache, sign out a provider, change UI copy, migrate source state, deploy, release or cut over.

A-007/A-016, O-023, exact destructive UX/policy, physical encrypted persistence, provider adapters, hosted resources, staging credentials, production profiling and production authorization remain outside this boundary.

verification.expected: Exact synthetic summaries keep all four work classes distinct; clean zero, pending sync-first and exact-confirmed destructive requests produce only their typed dispositions, while cancellation produces no request and no backend call.

Summary, confirmation and all request dispositions round-trip byte-identically with exact environment/Principal/Account/revision/time/count/fingerprint evidence and no provider, credential, path, payload or server-success claim.

Invalid time, clean-with-pending, missing/mismatched/stale destructive confirmation, changed environment/Principal/Account/count/revision/fingerprint and malformed evidence fail atomically with stable bounded diagnostic codes.

A deterministic reference AccountSessionEnding port receives only policy-ready requests: pending clean refuses, sync-first remains incomplete until a fresh zero summary, exact destructive confirmation passes, a changed summary refuses, cancellation does not call, and a failing port yields no false completion.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, provider/source-contamination and generated-contract checks, the complete target suite, both target builds and clean artifacts without changing an application project or claiming physical cleanup, Auth, provider, migration or production behavior.

notes: Decision-independent Phase 1 safety contract only. Canonical specs and reviewed architecture already require ordinary logout to preserve accepted offline work, sync-first to await authoritative/resolved outcomes, and destructive removal to use exact explicit confirmation. Exact UX copy/policy, A-007 Auth, A-016 offline lease, O-023 media retention, physical persistence/cleanup, schema/RLS/Sync/provider, app/MCP, source migration, hosted resources, production access and cutover remain fully open or gated because this boundary performs none of them.
